finding.title: Fix the stale "50%" coverage-floor comment in ci.yml (actual floor is 60%)
finding.why: The section header comment says the floor is 50%, but the step name ('Assert coverage floor ≥ 60%') and the enforced FLOOR=60 variable both say 60% — someone raised the floor and updated the step but not the section comment. Low-impact (the enforced value is correct and stricter than the comment implies) but misleads anyone skimming section headers to understand the pipeline.
finding.recommendation: Update the comment to '(60% line coverage, always enforced)'.
acceptance_criteria: The section-6 comment states the same percentage as the FLOOR variable.

finding.title: Remove the hardcoded personal PATH and silenced stderr in emit-fixtures
finding.why: This target hardcodes an absolute, author-specific local path (`/home/daniel/flutter/bin`) that doesn't exist on any other contributor's machine or CI runner, and pipes the underlying script's stderr to /dev/null with no exit-code check beyond Make's default abort-on-error. If `dart run tool/emit_fixture_payloads.dart` fails for any reason, the committed fixture `functions/test/fixtures/write_payloads.json` gets truncated (the `>` redirection opens/truncates the file before the command runs) with zero visible diagnostic — a developer sees only a bare 'make: *** Error N', not why, and could easily commit the now-empty fixture.
finding.recommendation: Drop the hardcoded PATH prefix (rely on the environment's own PATH, consistent with every other target in this Makefile) and remove `2>/dev/null` so failures are diagnosable.
acceptance_criteria: emit-fixtures contains no hardcoded absolute path and surfaces stderr on failure.

finding.title: Delete the now-vestigial integration_test/.gitkeep placeholder
finding.why: .gitkeep files exist solely to keep an otherwise-empty directory tracked by git. learning_tracker/integration_test/ has contained a real, tracked file (app_test.dart) since that test was added, so the .gitkeep no longer serves any purpose — pure clutter.

finding.title: Add value-type and string-size checks to firestore.rules' hasOnly() snapshot-collection whitelists

evidence.quote:
allow create, update: if isOwner(uid)
            && request.resource.data.keys().hasOnly([

allow create, update: if isOwner(uid)
            && request.resource.data.keys().hasOnly([

allow create, update: if isOwner(uid)
            && request.resource.data.keys().hasOnly([

finding.why: stage_definitions, curriculum_tracks, bookmarks, learning_order, goals, import_metadata, profile_programs and study_day_configs all gate create/update with `keys().hasOnly([...])` and nothing else -- no type check, no `size()` cap on any string field. A malicious or buggy client can write a multi-megabyte string into any allow-listed field (e.g. goals free-text fields), bloating every synced device's listener payload indefinitely, or write the wrong type where the Dart codec expects a specific one, surfacing only as a runtime cast failure on every device that later syncs the doc.
finding.recommendation: Add `is string && size() <= N` (or the appropriate type check) for at least the free-text fields in each collection, matching the pattern completions already uses for `points`.
acceptance_criteria: A create/update to goals with an oversized or wrong-typed field is denied, proven in functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs.

finding.title: Split allow list from allow read in firestore.rules to cap request.query.limit

evidence.quote: allow read: if isOwner(uid) || hasActiveTutorAccess(uid, profileId);
allow read: if isOwner(uid) || hasActiveTutorAccess(uid, profileId);
allow read: if isOwner(uid) || hasActiveTutorAccess(uid, profileId);

finding.why: `allow read` grants both `get` and `list` under the identical condition on every match block in the file (learner_profiles, completions, streak_events, learning_ledger, points_ledger, and every other subcollection); none constrains `request.query.limit`, so nothing stops an unbounded query. This matters most for the tutor cross-user read path: a compromised or custom client authenticated as an active tutor can issue one unlimited `.get()` query across a child's entire completions/learning_ledger history.
finding.recommendation: Split `allow read` into `allow get` (unchanged) and `allow list` (same condition && request.query.limit <= 500) on at least the per-profile event collections (completions, streak_events, learning_ledger, points_ledger).
acceptance_criteria: functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs asserts a list query with an unbounded/501+ limit against completions is denied while limit(500) succeeds.
